::: {.callout-note}
## Can you use cloud services?

For any project, you should always check whether using cloud services like GitHub and GitLab is suitable before you upload any code.

It may be, for instance, that the terms of a project mean the repo needs to be private (at least to begin with) or you need to consider what the licence terms need to be.
:::

## Git

[Git](https://git-scm.com/) can be used for version control to track and manage changes to code.

::: {.callout-tip}
For collaborative work, committing frequently and following the principles of [trunk-based development](https://www.atlassian.com/continuous-delivery/continuous-integration/trunk-based-development) can help ensure this minimises code divergence.
:::

## GitHub

REG has a [GitHub organisation](https://github.com/Bristol-REG) that you can use to create collaborative repositories.

You can request access by contacting [jgi-reseng@bristol.ac.uk](mailto:jgi-reseng@bristol.ac.uk).
Whilst at the University you can also access [additional education benefits](https://education.github.com/) on GitHub.

::: {.callout-note}
## Organisation or personal repo?

Using an organisation repo is recommended for larger or long-running projects.
This is helpful for continuity if there is a change in the staff working on the project.

For smaller projects, a repo under your personal profile is fine.
:::

## Data

You can also version control data but this is more unusual (raw or source data is generally considered read-only).

One data version control tool is [DVC](https://dvc.org/).
